newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends lower, gilts active, yields firm.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends lower, gilts active, yields firm.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday in the 9.50-9.75 percent range, down from the day's opening level of 9.75-10.25 percent, dealers said.
"Most of the deals were in the range of 9.75 percent to 10 percent", a dealer said. "Borrowers were quoting in the region of 9.00 percent to 9.50 percent," he said.
Yield on securities were firm, with little movement in the short term paper, dealers said.
Active securities included 13.62 percent 1998 at 13.60 percent at a price range of 100.25 rupees to 100.30 rupees and 13.70 percent 1999 at 13.75 percent, dealers said.
Market also saw deals in 91-day t-bills maturing in August at 9.0 percent, September at 9.60 percent and the 364 day t-bill maturing on 18 July, 1997 at 12.95 percent, dealers said.

There was no activity in certificates of deposit or commercial paper because of uneven trend in call rates and the expectation of firming of call rates in the coming weeks, corporate brokers said. "We expect the yield to go up by 100 to 150 basis point in near future," one broker said.
Inter-corporate deposit market was dull, with a handful of deals in the region of 17.0-19.0 percent for blue chip companies.
